newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expected to go ahead with UES bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia expected to go ahead with UES bond issue.

text.p: A Western source familiar with the planned convertible bond issue for Russia's Unified Energy System said on Tuesday the government would go ahead with the plan despite potential reservations by UES.
"The days when you had to strike a deal with each and every company being privatised or share proceeds of the privatisation are one or two years over," said the source.
"The shares belong to the government and it can sell."
Russia's State Property Committee said last month it would privatise a 7.50 percent stake in the national power company owned by the government through an issue of convertible bonds later this year.
But supporters of the bond are eager for the management of UES to take a positive approach to the bond, the price of which could otherwise be negatively affected.

"If UES are going to be proactive for it, that will help (the price)," said one Westerner. "UES support is an important part of the deal. The fact that the government is seller will help to get some leverage from the company."

UES president Anatoly Dyakov last month ruled out increasing the approximately 20 percent company stake held by foreigners, an important market for the convertible bonds, but has not commented publicly since then.
The company has declined to comment on the deal recently. Market sources say RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) may not have decided what policy to pursue.
The government will keep a 51 percent stake in UES until the end of 1998 but has an additional 8.5 percent stake to sell.
Participants are putting together details of the plan which will be probably be issued next week.
CS First Boston will be bookrunner for the deal, which will be lead managed by ABN AMRO Rothschild, Brunswick, Flemings and Russian banks MFK and Menatep.
UES is one of Russia's most liquid shares. Shares traded on Tuesday evening at $0.0729.
